MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L10·N11570unmasked layer
This neuron never truly activates positively — its output is negative everywhere in ordinary text and only rises to ~0 on the `<|begin_of_text|>` token, so it functions as a document-start/BOS detector (equivalently, an always-on negative bias suppressed hardest mid-sentence, e.g. on word-continuation suffixes like "-eting"/"-ing" and function words).

This neuron sits at a moderate baseline across informal second-person/first-person prose and spikes sharply on the token that launches a stock idiomatic clause right after a pronoun or comma — e.g. "at" in "at the same time"/"at least once", "you"/"never" in "you (never) know", "I" in "as I speak", "are" in "you are responsible" — i.e. a structural position at the start of a formulaic predicate/phrase rather than a semantic category.
